subject: Dedicated capacity ramp plan — phased onramp proposal
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@orionai.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity ramp plan — phased onramp proposal

Hi Samantha,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our discussion, attached is an initial stepwise onramp we think maps well to Orion's traffic profile and deployment milestones (attachment: ORION_dedicated_ramp_v1.pdf). High level: a three-stage GPU/TPM ramp over 9 months to reach target steady-state capacity.

Quick summary:
- Month 0–3: Pilot — 20 GPUs / baseline TPM allocations for validation and KV population
- Month 4–6: Growth — incremental increase to 60% target (40 GPUs)
- Month 7–9: Full-rate — remaining capacity to reach agreed steady state (65 GPUs)

Questions for you:
- Preferred billing cadence (monthly invoice vs. annual prepay)?
- Any procurement constraints we should pre-lock (PO timing, billing contact, preferred contract term)?
- Would you like us to propose a phased-credit schedule that releases committed credits as you hit rollout milestones?

Next step: if this looks directionally correct, I can share a pricing sketch and a staged credit release structure by Friday.

Best,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0192

Marissa —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the clear staging. A couple of immediate notes from our side:
- We favor annual prepay for predictability but need to understand the tradeoffs on unit price vs. cash impact.
- Can you define what you mean by "TPM allocations" in practical terms for our SREs (how does this map to GPU counts and expected latency)?
- Procurement is cc'd — they'll want a draft SOW and a proposal showing credit release tied to milestones.

Can your team propose a 12- and 24-month prepay option with equivalent staged credit releases? We can then run the numbers internally and revert.

Thanks,
Samantha

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ramp plan — phased onramp proposal

Samantha —

Thanks — I pushed a short spreadsheet (ORION_dedicated_ramp_v2.xlsx) that shows two pricing paths: 12-month annual prepay and 24-month annual prepay, both with the same 3-stage ramp but different term discounts. High-level bullets from the sheet:

- 12-month prepay: 10% term discount, credits released 50/30/20 across the three milestones (pilot / growth / full-rate)
- 24-month prepay: 15% term discount, credits released 40/35/25 (front-loaded slightly less to reduce cash pressure)
- Monthly invoicing option available but unit rates are ~20% higher vs. annual prepay

Milestone triggers we suggest for credit release:
1) Pilot acceptance (load test pass + KV cache warm)
2) Production traffic >50% of target for 14 days
3) Full-rate steady state for 30 days

Aditya — looping you in for the price math and to propose amortization options if Orion wants to smooth recognition across quarters. Rishi — would appreciate your thoughts on SLA-related credit mechanics (if the ramp timing shifts).

If this direction works, we can draft a short SOW and a DocuSign-ready contract for procurement to review.

Best,
Marissa

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.inference>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@orionai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference>, Orion AI Procurement <procurement@orionai.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ramp plan — phased onramp proposal

Samantha / team —

Quick pricing summary (sketch):
- List unit (monthly): $12,800 / GPU-equivalent (baseline).
- 12-month annual prepay: list less 10% => $11,520 / GPU-eq (billed up-front or net-30 as part of an annual prepayschedule).
- 24-month annual prepay: list less 15% => $10,880 / GPU-eq.

Suggested staged-credit mechanics (flexible):
- Credits issued as account balance and drawn against usage automatically.
- For annual prepay, we can structure partial release: 40% on pilot acceptance, 35% at growth milestone, 25% at full-rate (24-mo option) — or 50/30/20 for 12-mo.
- If ramp is slower than agreed, unused credits remain on account and are refundable within a narrow window or convertible to a reduced committed baseline (we can add a 6-month amortization carve-out).

On SLA / ramp guarantees: we generally avoid strict financial SLAs tied to ramp cadence, but we can offer a ramp-miss credit pool (capped) that vests only if Redwood is responsible for the delay. Rishi / legal can scope the exact language.

One operational note: to map "TPM" to GPU-eq we use a running profiler (we can share a sample trace) — for contracting we typically define a GPU-eq baseline and attach a short attachment describing profiling assumptions. Happy to run a call with your SREs.

—Aditya

From: Tom O'Neill <tom.oneill@orionai.com>

Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 09:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ramp plan — phased onramp proposal

Aditya / Marissa —

Procurement here. A few items we need to see in the next draft to move to legal review:
1) Firm ramp dates tied to credit releases and a clear definition of what constitutes "Pilot acceptance" (test criteria).
2) A ramp-miss remedy: we prefer a contractual credit that accrues against next invoice (not a refund). Please show an example calculation and a cap.
3) Clarify "refund window" language — we want clarity on how unused credits are handled at the 12- and 24-month marks.
4) Please attach your SOW template with redlines. See ours attached (SOW_template_redlines.docx).

Also: can you confirm the specific number of GPU-equivalents tied to the TPM ceilings in the v2 sheet? Our finance team needs the $/GPU-eq numbers to model cost-of-goods.

Tom O'Neill
VP, Procurement, Orion AI
procurement@orionai.com

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity ramp plan — phased onramp proposal

Tom / Samantha —

Thanks for the clarity. Proposed compromise to unblock legal & procurement:
- Ramp schedule (firm dates to be agreed in SOW): three stages at months 0, 4, and 8. Credit releases tied to: (1) pilot acceptance checklist, (2) sustained >50% traffic for 14 days, (3) 30-day steady-state.
- Financial terms: 24-month annual prepay with a 15% term discount if signed by 30 Sep 2026; credit release 60/30/10 by default OR an alternate 40/35/25 on request (we're willing to switch to reduce front-loaded cash impact).
- Ramp-miss remedy: 5% service credit (applied to next invoice) for any milestone missed due to Redwood delivery delays; cap = 20% of annual committed spend.
- Unused credits at the 12/24 month mark: refundable within 30 days or convertible to a 12-month rolling commitment at the same unit price (to avoid immediate churn).

Next steps:
1) Marissa / Aditya to deliver a redline-ready SOW and a sample contract with the above mechanics by Thursday, 18 Jun.
2) Tom / Procurement to mark up and return within 5 business days.
3) We will prepare a DocuSign envelope (link below) once terms are near-final for signature.
